summary: Final results are in, with Netanyahu's camp ahead but short of a majority; Herzog's two days of consultations open Wednesday evening, Nov 4, starting with the smaller parties, and his office says further rounds are possible. Eisenkot, Bennett, Lapid, Liberman and Golan back Eisenkot for the mandate, and Ynet projects he will receive more recommendations than Netanyahu, but the bloc has not said how it would reach a majority without Arab parties, which Liberman rejects. Religious Zionism and, per Israel National News, Shas's rabbinic council back Netanyahu, while UTJ has not committed to a recommendation. Netanyahu insists he should lead any broad government, while Eisenkot says Netanyahu lacks a majority and the opposition will form the government.

phase.now: Final results published; Herzog's consultations open Wednesday, Nov 4 at 5 pm with Religious Zionism, ending with Likud on Thursday evening
phase.next: Herzog will ask each faction whom it recommends and then choose a candidate for the mandate; his office does not rule out a second round. The new Knesset is sworn in on Nov 10.

scenarios.name: Netanyahu's Right-Religious Bloc
scenarios.note: His existing partners. On Nov 2 Netanyahu said publicly he wants Shas, Otzma Yehudit and Religious Zionism in any future government and that the public does not want one dependent on Ra'am and the Joint List. Without a majority, he needs defectors or a new partner from the other side.

blockers.text: Liberman urged Likud MKs to revolt against Netanyahu and says he won't sit with him.

scenarios.name: Change Bloc With Arab Parties
scenarios.note: Championed by Yair Golan, who met Lapid and then Abbas on Oct 29; the Times of Israel says he is the only Jewish-led bloc leader openly backing a coalition with Ra'am. Without Yisrael Beiteinu it falls short, and analysts told JTA the public is not ready for it. Channel 12 reports Abbas himself privately called an Eisenkot minority government with outside Arab support weak or impossible. AFP reports Eisenkot has not decided whether to seek a coalition relying on Arab parties, and the Joint List's Jabareen says he would back him from outside. A senior Joint List official told Walla on Nov 1 that the Joint List and Ra'am are expected to recommend Eisenkot to the president. Ynet reports Joint List and Ra'am leaders met in Nazareth on Nov 2 and will coordinate their recommendations. Ynet reports Bennett sides with Liberman against a government relying on Arab parties, believing it would collapse. On Nov 3 Golan met Joint List leaders and they agreed to keep coordinating, while the Times of Israel notes the bloc's joint statement gave no indication of how it would govern without Arab parties.

blockers.text: Liberman ruled out Ra'am, the Joint List and any minority government.
Eisenkot pledged a 'Zionist government' and has not backed the idea.
Ben-Gvir urged the Shin Bet to arrest Arab party leaders if there are legal grounds over alleged Qatari funding.
Ynet reports Bennett opposes any government reliant on Arab parties, expecting it to collapse.

scenarios.name: Change Bloc With Ra'am Only
scenarios.note: The 2021 Bennett–Lapid model. Ynet reports, citing unnamed sources, that Eisenkot authorized examining a minority government with Ra'am inside and UTJ abstaining, possibly as leverage in unity talks; Yashar says such reports are not issued on its behalf. It falls short of 61 and Liberman rejects any government dependent on Arab or Haredi parties. Unnamed sources tell Ynet that Liberman berated Eisenkot at a Saturday meeting, saying the minority-government push hurt the bloc.

blockers.text: Liberman ruled out Ra'am and said on Nov 2 he would oppose an Eisenkot minority government.
Ynet reports Bennett opposes any government reliant on Arab parties, expecting it to collapse.

scenarios.name: Change Bloc With Shas And UTJ
scenarios.note: No Arab parties needed, but the Haredi draft splits it. A source close to Eisenkot tells Ynet he is trying to bring Shas and UTJ into a government he leads, naming Liberman as the main obstacle. A senior UTJ official told Ynet the party would offer Eisenkot the premiership for draft exemptions, which clashes with his national-service condition; Shas is reported to be out. Unnamed senior UTJ figures say the party might back an Eisenkot government from outside without a draft law first, the Times of Israel reports. On Nov 2 Liberman declined to rule out cooperating with UTJ, saying the bloc will have to see what happens. Ynet reports on Nov 3 that Eisenkot is focusing on courting the Haredi parties and that Liberman has left the door open to talks on including them. The Jerusalem Post reports on Nov 3 that Shas and UTJ stress no decision has been made, with their rabbis due back around the start of consultations.

blockers.text: Haredi sources tell the Jerusalem Post that Deri won't join an opposition-led government without Likud.
Shas and UTJ say they won't join any government unless yeshiva students' exemptions are written into law.
Liberman pledged not to sit with Shas and UTJ, though on Nov 2 he declined to rule out cooperating with UTJ.
Eisenkot's core promise is national service for all.

scenarios.name: National Unity Government
scenarios.note: The Jerusalem Post reports Netanyahu-linked sources are promoting it, possibly with a rotating premiership and without Shas and UTJ. Kan cites Netanyahu associate Benny Biton as saying Netanyahu wants unity, and an unnamed Likud official named Herzog and Trump as guarantors for Eisenkot. Channel 12 reports Liberman wants Eisenkot to join Netanyahu, though not under his own banner. Who would lead it is the sticking point. Likud whip Ofir Katz told Army Radio the party opposes rotation and others can join the existing coalition. Channel 14 reports, citing unnamed sources, that Netanyahu has given up on unity talks and is preparing for a new election. Ynet reports Netanyahu told associates privately he is not ruling out any option, including rotation, and that Katz says unity is off if the opposition ousts Speaker Ohana. On Nov 2 Netanyahu said publicly he is open to a broad government with any party that does not support terrorism but that he should lead it; an associate told Ynet no unity proposal has yet been made. Israel Hayom reports a Likud source's assessment, not a negotiated offer, that Netanyahu could accept unity if he served about two years and then became president, with Eisenkot taking over.

blockers.text: Likud whip Ofir Katz said the party opposes a rotation of the premiership.
Eisenkot rules out serving under Netanyahu, including in a rotation.
Channel 12 reports Liberman still refuses to join a Netanyahu-led government, even as he urges Eisenkot to.
Ben-Gvir warned Netanyahu against a unity government with Eisenkot.

scenarios.name: Netanyahu Plus Bennett's Together
scenarios.note: Ideologically the closest fit, but Bennett and Lapid campaigned on replacing Netanyahu.

blockers.text: Bennett declared on election night that Netanyahu has lost.

מחל.stance: In his first public remarks since election night, Netanyahu said on Nov 2 he should lead any government, wants to keep Shas, Otzma Yehudit and Religious Zionism, and is open to a broad government with parties that don't support terrorism.
red_lines: No government that depends on Arab parties

דרך.stance: On Nov 3 Eisenkot and the other opposition leaders agreed to start coalition talks at once and reaffirmed backing him for the first mandate.
red_lines: Partners must accept his four principles

רק.stance: Bennett said on Nov 3 his whole party will work to help Eisenkot form a government and urged quickly replacing Speaker Ohana; Ynet reports he opposes a government relying on Arab parties.
red_lines: No government reliant on Arab parties (per Ynet)

אמת.stance: Golan met Joint List leaders Jabareen and Tibi on Nov 3, and the two sides agreed to keep coordinating toward a change government.

ל.stance: Liberman said on Nov 3 a government can be formed without Arab parties and another election must be prevented; he will recommend Eisenkot and won't sit with Netanyahu.

שס.stance: Israel National News reports Shas's Council of Torah Sages decided to recommend Netanyahu after he committed to regularizing yeshiva students' status.

ג.stance: Ynet reports UTJ decided not to recommend any candidate for now and will weigh replacing Speaker Ohana only after a concrete Eisenkot proposal; Goldknopf favors backing Eisenkot while Porush is skeptical.

ב.stance: Ben-Gvir attacked the idea of a government with the Joint List after Jabareen declined to call Hamas a terror group; he rejects unity with Eisenkot and backs keeping a right-wing government.

ט.stance: Religious Zionism said on Nov 3 it will recommend Netanyahu as head of the largest party and bloc and urge the left to drop boycotts for a broad Jewish government.

עם.stance: Ra'am met the Joint List in Nazareth on Nov 2; Ynet reports the two will coordinate their recommendations and appear likely to back Eisenkot.

ודם.stance: Joint List leaders Jabareen and Tibi met Golan on Nov 3 and agreed to keep coordinating toward a change government, a Democrats statement said.

timeline.text: Says Netanyahu lacks a majority and that the opposition bloc will form the next government, the Jerusalem Post reports.
Ahead of the consultations, Ynet projects Eisenkot is poised to receive more recommendations than Netanyahu.
The attorney general asked the Shin Bet to report on its probe into Arab parties' alleged electoral fraud, saying no evidence had yet been submitted, AFP reports.
Herzog's office says he will start with smaller parties to hear all views and may hold further rounds of consultations before choosing a candidate.
Joint List leader Jabareen says the opposition must accept political reality and join forces with Arab parties to remove Netanyahu, AFP reports.
Haaretz's live coverage reports Likud is weighing whether to refuse to recognize the election results.
Anadolu reports Shas will recommend Netanyahu to form the next government.
After their meeting, Eisenkot and the other opposition leaders vow to form an emergency government as soon as possible, the Jerusalem Post reports.
Announces it will recommend Netanyahu to Herzog and call on left-wing parties to end boycotts and join a broad Jewish government.
The Zehut chair says he will also recommend Netanyahu but ask Herzog to push for new elections, claiming the vote's integrity was compromised.
The party's Council of Torah Sages backs recommending Netanyahu after his commitment on yeshiva students' status, Israel National News reports.
Eisenkot, Bennett, Golan and Liberman agree to launch coalition talks immediately and reaffirm backing Eisenkot for the first mandate.
Channel 12 reports the leaders discussed backing Lapid for Knesset speaker and will decide by Monday.
Says his party will mobilize all its efforts to help Eisenkot form a government and urges quickly replacing Speaker Ohana.
Meets Joint List leaders Jabareen and Tibi; the sides agree to keep coordinating toward a change government.
Says a government can be formed without Arab parties and another election must be prevented.
Arriving at the opposition meeting, says Netanyahu must be removed and warns of a dangerous attempt to undermine the results.
Likud asks to delay certification of the results, citing an interference probe; the elections committee chair rejects the request.
Haredi party representatives stress no decision has been made on recommendations, with their rabbis due back as consultations begin.
Senior bloc figures tell Ynet their most urgent task is controlling the Knesset: replacing Speaker Ohana, forming the Arrangements Committee and repealing coalition laws.
Ynet reports Eisenkot wants a speaker from his own party, while Liberman and Bennett favor Lapid.
Ynet reports Bennett sides with Liberman against a government reliant on Arab parties, believing it would collapse.
In his first public remarks on the government since election night, says he should lead any broad government and wants Shas, Otzma Yehudit and Religious Zionism kept in it.
Says the public does not want a government dependent on Ra'am and the Joint List.
His office publishes the consultation schedule: Religious Zionism, Shas and Yisrael Beiteinu on Wednesday; UTJ through Likud on Thursday.
Leaders of the two Arab parties meet in Nazareth and will coordinate their recommendations, Ynet reports.
The UTJ figure tells Radio Jerusalem the party does not rule out cooperating with Arab parties.
Eisenkot, Bennett, Lapid, Liberman and Golan will meet Tuesday at 11:30 in Herzliya, their first joint meeting since the results, JFeed reports.
Channel 12's Amit Segal reports Shas has settled on recommending Netanyahu for prime minister.
The Shas Council elder denies reports he was approached about backing Eisenkot.
